name: bas55
desc: Minimal BASIC programming language interpreter as defined by ECMA-55
why: A faithful ECMA-55 BASIC interpreter is a delightful time capsule of an old-school language.

brief.what_it_is: bas55 is a free-software implementation of the Minimal BASIC programming language as defined by the ECMA-55 standard. It ships as an interpreter plus an editor that includes line renumbering. The homepage describes it as a complete system, and the Windows package is a zip of the same tools. I did not see documented input or output formats, so the details of running a program are not in the pages I read.
brief.why_it_exists: The README gives no explicit motivation. It presents bas55 as an implementation of the ECMA-55 Minimal BASIC standard, and the homepage says it has been tested against the National Bureau of Standards Minimal BASIC test programs.
brief.install_notes: The homepage offers a source tarball (bas55-2.0.tar.gz), a Windows zip (bas55v20.zip), and older versions back to 1.01. The README I read has no build steps, dependencies, or first-run instructions, and I did not open the online manual, so those details are unknown. The binary name is bas55 according to the Homebrew metadata.
brief.standout: It is a faithful, small implementation of an old standard that is rarely implemented today, and it bundles an editor with line renumbering alongside the interpreter. The author also tested it against the NBS Minimal BASIC test suite, which suggests a serious conformance goal.
brief.status: Unknown in the strict sense: I saw no last-commit date or release date. The homepage lists version 2.0 as the latest tarball and links to a NEWS file and to a dated NBS test set from July 2021, and the GitHub repo is linked from it. That points to a project that is still being looked after but not very actively developed.
brief.caveats: The README is thin and I did not follow the manual link, so usage details are missing. The Windows package is a separate zip, not a Homebrew-only build. The homepage's mention of a compiler for x86-64 Linux refers to a different project by John Gatewood Ham, not to bas55. Licensing is GPL v3 or later. Bug reports go to a personal email address.

judge.reason: A conformance-minded ECMA-55 interpreter offers a rare, hands-on look at the constraints and design of standardized Minimal BASIC.

entry.title: bas55
entry.tldr: A small interpreter for ECMA-55 Minimal BASIC, the 1978 standard, tested against the US National Bureau of Standards conformance programs.
entry.deeper_look:
bas55 implements Minimal BASIC as defined by the ECMA-55 standard. It provides an interpreter and an editor with line renumbering. The homepage calls it a complete system, and a Windows build is offered as a zip of the same tools.

Minimal BASIC is the stripped-down core of the language: numbered lines, a handful of statements, no frills. ECMA-55 pins that core down in a short formal document, which makes it a rare case of BASIC having a real specification. Most BASICs that people remember are vendor dialects, each different. This one follows the written standard.

The author says the interpreter was tested against the National Bureau of Standards Minimal BASIC test programs, so conformance seems to be a real goal rather than a nostalgia gesture. That makes it a way to see what BASIC looked like before dialects diverged, and a small example of how a language standard gets checked against an implementation.

The README is thin and gives no motivation or usage walkthrough, so the online manual is the place to learn how to run programs.

try_this.what_happens: Prints the interpreter's usage and options, the quickest way to learn how to run a program file.

entry.whats_unique: Few modern tools implement Minimal BASIC as the ECMA-55 standard defines it. This one checks itself against the NBS conformance test suite and bundles a renumbering editor.
entry.caveats: The README has no usage steps, so you will need the online manual, and the project appears maintained but not very actively developed.
